correctness.rationale: The fold normalization reduces each held-out log e-value to a two-Gaussian quadratic form. Conditional Gaussian integration gives the exact component \(q\)-moment and its strict integrability boundary. Jensen supplies finiteness for the average when \(q\ge1\), positivity supplies necessity, and \(x^q\le1+x\) covers \(0\le q\le1\). The unequal-split statement follows from the same exact normalization. The log-moment claim follows because the log average lies between the minimum and maximum quadratic forms. The packaged exact-arithmetic checker verifies determinant and threshold algebra.

value.rationale: This gives a motivated all-orders stability classification for a procedure whose infinite cross-fit variance has been explicitly highlighted as puzzling in the literature. It identifies exactly how many folds are needed for each integer moment, explains the golden-ratio cross-fit tail boundary, and gives a new moment-robustness reason for balanced two-way splitting while separating raw-e-value tails from benign log-statistic moments.
